assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors turn a defined chemical reaction (cytidine and adenosine deamination on a Cas-bound single-stranded DNA window) into a programmable tool for single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks. Chemically elegant, with broad use in research and in clinical therapy for genetic disease; it also asks directly how the cell's own repair of deaminated bases (uracil, inosine) shapes the outcome.
assessment.attribution: David Liu led the work and the concept, and Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors, which needed evolution of an artificial TadA deaminase) were the lead experimentalists. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) were parallel and independent, so a three-person configuration omits them. I would defend Liu with Komor and Gaudelli as the most natural unit, and I am uncertain how others would weigh the Japanese contribution.
assessment.maturity: About ten years since the first report; independently reproduced in many labs, extended to mitochondrial editing, and in human clinical use. Recognition looks timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to treat base editing and prime editing as one prize block, or recognise CRISPR-derived tools only after the 2020 prize has aged further.
Attribution to Kondo/Nishida versus Komor/Gaudelli is a judgment call.
Long-term clinical safety data and off-target deamination profiles are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, via bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues such as the thalidomide-class degraders, converts a biological process into small-molecule chemistry and opens targets that inhibitors cannot reach. The conceptual shift from occupancy-driven to event-driven pharmacology is substantial, and several degraders are in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and founded PROTACs (Sakamoto, Kim, Crews, Deshaies, 2001); Ciulli contributed the first VHL-based small-molecule PROTACs and structural mechanism. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, cereblon as thalidomide target) is a separate discovery with its own claim, so the candidate is a compound one. I would pick the PROTAC trio but accept that glue discovery may need its own recognition.
assessment.maturity: Two decades old at concept stage, with strong independent confirmation and pharmaceutical adoption, but late-stage clinical proof for approved PROTAC drugs is still limited.
uncertainties: Compound candidate in which PROTACs and glue degraders may deserve different laureates.
Few approved PROTAC drugs so far; clinical benefit is not yet established beyond phase 3 readouts.
Sakamoto and Kim credit for the 2001 proof of concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids in vivo and rewrite codon assignments, giving biologists an exact chemical probe of proteins in living cells. It is a general, widely used tool that turned a biological machine into a controlled reaction system.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the method (Wang, Brock, Schultz 2001) and Lei Wang was first author of the foundational work; Chin extended it to multiple orthogonal pairs, quadruplet codons and synthetic genomes. Yokoyama and Mehl are additional contributors. Schultz, Wang and Chin is a plausible set, though the order of credit between Wang and Chin is arguable.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades old, replicated in bacteria, yeast, mammalian cells and animals, and used in therapeutics (site-specific conjugates). Fully mature.
uncertainties: Prize-set boundaries between Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or primarily synthetic biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase carries out one of the most difficult reactions in biology, N2 reduction at the FeMo-cofactor. Crystal structures (including the interstitial carbide), spectroscopy and kinetics give a mechanistic chemical picture of an enzyme crucial to the nitrogen cycle. As an enzymologist I value its clear mechanism, though the full catalytic cycle remains incompletely resolved.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the structural work (MoFe protein in 1992, cofactor atoms later); Einsle contributed the high-resolution cofactor with the central light atom and later structures; Seefeldt and Dean contributed mechanism, with Ribbe on cofactor biosynthesis. Defensible trio is Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, but I do not independently verify who did what in the cofactor-assignment papers.
assessment.maturity: Structures are confirmed in several laboratories and species; recent cryo-EM structures under turnover conditions add mechanistic detail. Core claims are stable, although the central atom and the substrate-binding site continue to be refined.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 binding and reduction (E4 state, hydride involvement) still debated.
Complex attribution among five credited people, and a possibility that structure and mechanism deserve separate credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation gives a chemoselective, well-defined reaction to join unprotected peptide segments, with expressed protein ligation extending it to semisynthesis. It enabled total chemical synthesis of proteins, site-specific modifications and many mechanistic studies, and fits my interest in turning biological questions into precise chemical reactions.
assessment.attribution: Dawson, Muir, Kent (Science 1994) are the decisive trio for native chemical ligation, with Muir for expressed protein ligation. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are significant on later developments; they are not required for the founding discovery.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years old, universally used, and independently reproduced; if anything the recognition is late.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier Nobel recognition of peptide synthesis and the fact that the discovery is now mainly a tool.
Credit for the Kent group vs the Dawson/Muir contribution is shared in a single paper.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics (shotgun sequencing, isotope-coded affinity tags, high-resolution quantitative workflows, SILAC) made it possible to measure thousands of proteins and modifications; this is the measurement foundation for much of modern cell biology. I trust discoveries that rest on analytical measurement, and my own nucleotide-pool measurements depend on LC-MS/MS.
assessment.attribution: Mann (quantification, high-resolution workflows, SILAC), Aebersold (ICAT, targeted and SWATH-style measurement) and Yates (shotgun, MudPIT, database searching) are the clearest trio. Hunt, Gygi and Heck also made decisive contributions, so the set is selective and contentious.
assessment.maturity: Methods are mature and widely validated in thousands of laboratories; recognition is timely or somewhat overdue. The 2002 prize recognised ESI and MALDI, which is a separate step.
uncertainties: Large number of strong contributors and no obvious cut-off.
Prior mass-spectrometry prizes may be viewed as already covering enabling ionization.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule electrical readout of nucleic acids through protein pores has delivered long-read sequencing and a new class of analytical devices. It requires chemistry of pore engineering (Bayley), enzyme-controlled translocation, and signal interpretation, and works for DNA, RNA and modifications.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer demonstrated the first single-stranded nucleic-acid translocation (1996); Akeson showed discrimination and enzymatic ratcheting; Bayley engineered pores and showed single-base detection. A fair set of three is difficult because all five are credible.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices have been used for more than a decade and the approach is confirmed independently, although accuracy for some uses is still improving.
uncertainties: Founding discovery and engineering contributions are spread across five names.
Branton is deceased, which constrains the credit configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's covalent targeting of the mutant KRAS G12C switch-II pocket, together with chemical genetics of analogue-sensitive kinases, created clear chemical tools and the first route to drugging a long-undruggable oncogene, leading to approved drugs. It combines mechanism, general approach, and large medical consequences.
assessment.attribution: The list credits a single person, which simplifies attribution; however, subsequent drug development involved Amgen, Mirati and others, and the nearby work of Ostrem, Shokat and colleagues was jointly done. Single-laureate credit is internally clean, but I cannot verify the details of the cooperating groups.
assessment.maturity: The first report dates from 2013, with approved drugs from 2021; the validation is strong but long-term benefit and resistance are still under study, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Resistance mechanisms and durability of clinical benefit.
Kinase chemical genetics and KRAS may be two separate contributions.
The committee may want more time before honouring a still-evolving clinical story.
